title: Hirak and pro-democracy march in central Algiers
participants_original: Algerie360: hundreds; one embedded post title says one hundred. Al Jazeera: 400–500. Maghreb Émergent: about one hundred in an earlier spontaneous march.
threshold_50_evidence: At least 100 reported in Algiers city centre (DZA202010_S004, DZA202010_S005); Al Jazeera reports 400–500 (DZA202010_S001).

start_date.summary: All four reports date the Algiers march to 5 October 2020.

location.summary: Reports place the march in central Algiers, including Didouche Mourad and downtown streets.

demands.summary: Reports describe demands for political change, a civil state and release of Hirak detainees.

participants_original.summary: Reports give estimates ranging from about one hundred to 400–500; the lower numeric estimate is retained as minimum.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Independent contemporaneous reports provide estimates above 50.

protester_violence.summary: No source establishes whether protesters used violence; unknown.

state_response.summary: Reports say police dispersed marchers and arrested participants in Algiers.

notes: Treats the Algiers city-centre action as one event despite differences in crowd estimates and multiple processions; three local reports place spontaneous activity around Didouche Mourad. AFP is credited only for an Al Jazeera photo; Euronews is a distinct AFP byline on a separate issue and is not used here.
open_questions: Confirm whether early spontaneous gathering and later march were one continuous action or separate local actions.
Verify onset/continuation against September and November dossiers before approval.

title: Hirak commemorative protests reported outside Algiers

start_date.summary: Le Matin reports protests in these localities on 5 October.

location.summary: Reports mention other areas across Algeria; Le Matin names Annaba, Constantine, Jijel, Oran and Akbou.

demands.summary: Reports connect actions to Hirak slogans, release of detainees and opposition to the regime.

participants_original.summary: No turnout estimates for these named locations; unknown.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No location-specific evidence of 50 participants; eligibility remains pending threshold.

protester_violence.summary: No report establishes protester violence at these locations; unknown.

state_response.summary: Le Matin reports arrests and mistreatment across some named localities; the scope is not sufficiently specific to assign all details to each town.

notes: Kept separate from Algiers because nationally organized coordination and local event boundaries are not established. Le Matin reports some arrests and mistreatment but gives no attendance estimates.
open_questions: Resolve event-level locations and attendance with local contemporary reporting.
Determine whether local actions were nationally organized as one event or separate actions.

title: Hirak mobilization and police dispersal in Vgayet (Béjaïa)
threshold_50_evidence: Report explicitly says several hundred mobilized at Vgayet (DZA202010_S007).

start_date.summary: The article reports marches on 2 and 3 October but does not identify which of the two days corresponds to the Vgayet crowd; month precision retained.

demands.summary: The march is identified as Hirak action; report describes a political protest and demands for the movement to remain active, but exact event demands need review.

participants_original.summary: Several hundred mobilized, in source wording.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Several hundred is clear qualitative evidence above 50.

protester_violence.summary: No protester violence is described; unknown.

state_response.summary: Police dispersed participants with tear gas and explicitly fired blank rounds; several arrests are reported.

notes: The source dates the multiple marches to 2–3 October but internally calls 3 October both Saturday and Tuesday; it does not map the counted Vgayet crowd to one exact day. “Blank rounds” supports shots fired but does not establish live ammunition.
open_questions: Resolve exact Vgayet gathering date and whether the crowd/action was one or multiple march events.
Clarify the movement’s specific state-directed demand at this location.

title: Hirak march in Kherrata demanding Khaled Tazaghart’s release
threshold_50_evidence: Report says thousands gathered and protested against the Algerian authorities (DZA202010_S007).

start_date.summary: Article gives 3 October as the date but conflicts over the weekday; calendar date retained provisionally with a date-quality flag.

location.summary: Article identifies Kherrata in eastern Kabylie.

demands.summary: The report says demonstrators demanded release of activist Khaled Tazaghart and protested against the Algerian authorities.

participants_original.summary: Thousands, as reported; no exact numeric estimate.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Thousands is clear qualitative evidence above 50.

protester_violence.summary: No report establishes protester violence at Kherrata; unknown.

state_response.summary: Specific state response to the Kherrata gathering is not reported; unknown.

notes: Source says “thousands”; no exact number is inferred. Article elsewhere dates marches to 2–3 October and calls 3 October Tuesday, inconsistent with its own Saturday reference.
open_questions: Verify date and whether this action was part of a broader multi-day Hirak episode.

title: Imceddalen march attempt and gathering demanding activists’ release

start_date.summary: Article dates the attempted march and follow-up gathering to 3 October.

demands.summary: After several activists were detained, demonstrators gathered at the police station to demand their release.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No evidence establishes 50 or more participants; pending threshold.

protester_violence.summary: Source reports tensions but does not describe protesters using violence; unknown.

state_response.summary: Police repressed the attempted march and detained activists; arrests and dispersal are supported.

notes: The later gathering outside the police station may be a distinct follow-up action; kept together provisionally pending event-boundary review.
open_questions: Determine whether the follow-up gathering is a distinct action and whether it reached 50 participants.

title: Women’s protest against femicide and gender-based violence in Algiers

start_date.summary: Euronews dates the Algiers demonstration to 8 October 2020.

location.summary: Euronews places the gathering in Algiers.

demands.summary: Women protested after a femicide and called for state protection mechanisms and shelters for victims of violence.

participants_original.summary: About one hundred women, as reported.

protester_violence.summary: No source evidence of protester violence; unknown.

notes: The policy demand concerns state protection and public response to gender-based violence; political_behavior_process is a provisional available code because the codebook has no dedicated GBV category.
open_questions: Review whether the protest’s demand maps to the supplied MM demand categories.
